prompt: A seven-panel photo strip of the same mountain cable-car station, panels side by side left to right. Each panel is numbered 1 to 7 in its top-left corner. In each panel a single kit bag of one solid flat colour stands in the middle of the scene, and a printed log slip pinned to the wall states what happened at that moment. In panel order the kit bag colours are MAROON, CREAM, OLIVE, NAVY, TURQUOISE, GREY, SCARLET. The log slips read WHISTLE BLOWN in panels 1, 2, 5 and NO WHISTLE in panels 3, 4, 6, 7. Now the rule about the enamel disc, which is a big plain shape of flat colour fixed well away from the kit bag. In each panel the enamel disc is the colour of the kit bag that stood there at the MOST RECENT EARLIER panel whose slip reads WHISTLE BLOWN. A panel's own slip never counts as earlier than itself. In the first panel there is no earlier panel at all, so there the enamel disc is left plain unpainted bare. I am deliberately not listing the answer anywhere in this request; work it out from the figures printed in the picture.
easy_question: This image was supposed to show a strip of separate numbered panels in a row, each panel showing one big single-coloured object standing in it and a printed slip of text on the wall. Ignoring artistic quality, and ignoring whether the details are right or wrong, does the image DEPICT that? Answer NO only if the picture is unrelated to that description or contains no such arrangement at all. Answer yes or no only.
